#!/bin/bash
# shellcheck source=scripts/helper_functions.sh
source "/home/steam/server/helper_functions.sh"

# shellcheck source=scripts/negative_delta_recovery.sh
source "/home/steam/server/negative_delta_recovery.sh"

if ! ValidateNegativeDeltaRecoverySetting; then
    LogError "PALWORLD_ALLOW_NEGATIVE_DELTA_TIME must be true or false."
    exit 1
fi

# Helper Functions for installation & updates
# shellcheck source=scripts/helper_install.sh
source "/home/steam/server/helper_install.sh"

dirExists "/palworld" || exit
isWritable "/palworld" || exit
isExecutable "/palworld" || exit

cd /palworld || exit

# Get the architecture using dpkg
architecture=$(dpkg --print-architecture)

IsInstalled
ServerInstalled=$?
if [ "$ServerInstalled" == 1 ]; then
    LogInfo "Server installation not detected."
    LogAction "Starting Installation"
    InstallServer
fi

# Always update on boot even if the server is installed, to prevent appmanifest issues
if [ "$ServerInstalled" == 0 ] && [ "${UPDATE_ON_BOOT,,}" == true ]; then
    if UpdateRequired; then
        rm /palworld/steamapps/appmanifest_2394010.acf
        InstallServer
    fi
fi

STARTCOMMAND=("./PalServer.sh")

#Validate Installation
if ! fileExists "${STARTCOMMAND[0]}"; then
    LogError "Server Not Installed Properly"
    exit 1
fi

# Check if the architecture is arm64
if [ "$architecture" == "arm64" ]; then
    # create an arm64 version of ./PalServer.sh

    cp ./PalServer.sh ./PalServer-arm64.sh
    
    sed -i "s|\(\"\$UE_PROJECT_ROOT\/Pal\/Binaries\/Linux\/PalServer-Linux-Shipping\" Pal \"\$@\"\)|LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/home/steam/steamcmd/linux64:\$LD_LIBRARY_PATH /usr/local/bin/box64 \1|" ./PalServer-arm64.sh
    chmod +x ./PalServer-arm64.sh
    STARTCOMMAND=("./PalServer-arm64.sh")
fi

isReadable "${STARTCOMMAND[0]}" || exit
if ! isExecutable "${STARTCOMMAND[0]}"; then
    LogWarn "Attempt to make \"${STARTCOMMAND[0]}\" executable"
    chmod +x "${STARTCOMMAND[0]}" || exit
    isExecutable "${STARTCOMMAND[0]}" || exit
fi

# Prepare Arguments
if [ -n "${PORT}" ]; then
    STARTCOMMAND+=("-port=${PORT}")
fi

if [ -n "${QUERY_PORT}" ]; then
    STARTCOMMAND+=("-queryport=${QUERY_PORT}")
fi

if [ "${COMMUNITY,,}" = true ]; then
    STARTCOMMAND+=("-publiclobby")
fi

if [ "${ENABLE_PERF_THREADING_ARGS,,}" = true ]; then
    STARTCOMMAND+=("-useperfthreads" "-NoAsyncLoadingThread" "-UseMultithreadForDS")
fi

if [ "${PALWORLD_ALLOW_NEGATIVE_DELTA_TIME,,}" = true ]; then
    STARTCOMMAND+=("-ini:Engine:[ConsoleVariables]:Pal.AllowNegativeDeltaTime=1")
fi

if [ -n "${WORKER_THREADS_SERVER}" ]; then
    STARTCOMMAND+=("-NumberOfWorkerThreadsServer=${WORKER_THREADS_SERVER}")
fi

# Backward compatibility (deprecated)
if [ "${MULTITHREADING,,}" = true ]; then
    LogWarn "MULTITHREADING is deprecated. Use ENABLE_PERF_THREADING_ARGS and WORKER_THREADS_SERVER instead."
    if [ "${ENABLE_PERF_THREADING_ARGS,,}" != true ]; then
        STARTCOMMAND+=("-useperfthreads" "-NoAsyncLoadingThread" "-UseMultithreadForDS")
    fi

    if [ -z "${WORKER_THREADS_SERVER}" ]; then
        STARTCOMMAND+=("-NumberOfWorkerThreadsServer=$(nproc --all)")
    fi
fi

if [ "${ENABLE_GAMEDATA_API,,}" = true ]; then
    STARTCOMMAND+=("-enable-gamedata-api")
fi

LogAction "Checking for available container updates"
container_version_check

if [ "${DISABLE_GENERATE_SETTINGS,,}" = true ]; then
  LogAction "GENERATING CONFIG"
  LogWarn "Env vars will not be applied due to DISABLE_GENERATE_SETTINGS being set to TRUE!"

  # shellcheck disable=SC2143
  if [ ! "$(grep -s '[^[:space:]]' /palworld/Pal/Saved/Config/LinuxServer/PalWorldSettings.ini)" ]; then
      LogAction "GENERATING CONFIG"
      mkdir -p /palworld/Pal/Saved/Config/LinuxServer || exit
      fileExists "/palworld/DefaultPalWorldSettings.ini" || exit
      cp "/palworld/DefaultPalWorldSettings.ini" "/palworld/Pal/Saved/Config/LinuxServer/PalWorldSettings.ini" || exit
  fi
else
  LogAction "GENERATING CONFIG"
  LogInfo "Using Env vars to create PalWorldSettings.ini"
  /home/steam/server/compile-settings.sh || exit
fi

if [ "${DISABLE_GENERATE_ENGINE,,}" = false ]; then
    /home/steam/server/compile-engine.sh || exit
fi

LogAction "GENERATING CRONTAB"
truncate -s 0  "/home/steam/server/crontab"

if [ "${BACKUP_ENABLED,,}" = true ]; then
    LogInfo "BACKUP_ENABLED=${BACKUP_ENABLED,,}"
    LogInfo "Adding cronjob for auto backups"
    echo "$BACKUP_CRON_EXPRESSION bash /usr/local/bin/backup" >> "/home/steam/server/crontab"
    supercronic -quiet -test -no-reap "/home/steam/server/crontab" || exit
fi

if [ "${AUTO_UPDATE_ENABLED,,}" = true ] && [ "${UPDATE_ON_BOOT}" = true ]; then
    LogInfo "AUTO_UPDATE_ENABLED=${AUTO_UPDATE_ENABLED,,}"
    LogInfo "Adding cronjob for auto updating"
    echo "$AUTO_UPDATE_CRON_EXPRESSION bash /usr/local/bin/update" >> "/home/steam/server/crontab"
    supercronic -quiet -test -no-reap "/home/steam/server/crontab" || exit
fi

if [ "${AUTO_REBOOT_ENABLED,,}" = true ] && [ "${REST_API_ENABLED,,}" = true ]; then
    LogInfo "AUTO_REBOOT_ENABLED=${AUTO_REBOOT_ENABLED,,}"
    LogInfo "Adding cronjob for auto rebooting via REST API"
    echo "$AUTO_REBOOT_CRON_EXPRESSION bash /home/steam/server/auto_reboot.sh" >> "/home/steam/server/crontab"
    supercronic -quiet -test -no-reap "/home/steam/server/crontab" || exit
fi

CRON_PID=""
if [ -s "/home/steam/server/crontab" ]; then
    supercronic -passthrough-logs -no-reap "/home/steam/server/crontab" &
    CRON_PID=$!
    LogInfo "Cronjobs started"
else
    LogInfo "No Cronjobs found"
fi

# Configure RCON settings.
# DEPRECATED: RCON will be removed in a future release.
cat >/home/steam/server/rcon.yaml  <<EOL
default:
  address: "127.0.0.1:${RCON_PORT}"
  password: "${ADMIN_PASSWORD}"
EOL

CHILD_PIDS=()
if PlayerLogging_isEnabled; then
    if [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]; then
        setpriv --reuid=steam --regid=steam --init-groups "${FORCE_CAPS[@]}" /home/steam/server/player_logging.sh &
    else
        /home/steam/server/player_logging.sh &
    fi
    CHILD_PIDS+=($!)
fi

LogAction "Starting Server"
DiscordMessage "Start" "${DISCORD_PRE_START_MESSAGE}" "success" "${DISCORD_PRE_START_MESSAGE_ENABLED}" "${DISCORD_PRE_START_MESSAGE_URL}"

echo "${STARTCOMMAND[*]}"
"${STARTCOMMAND[@]}"

LogAction "Ending Server"

if [ -n "$CRON_PID" ]; then
    LogInfo "Stopping cronjobs"
    kill -SIGTERM "$CRON_PID" 2>/dev/null
fi

if [ ${#CHILD_PIDS[@]} -ne 0 ]; then
    wait "${CHILD_PIDS[@]}"
fi

DiscordMessage "Stop" "${DISCORD_POST_SHUTDOWN_MESSAGE}" "failure" "${DISCORD_POST_SHUTDOWN_MESSAGE_ENABLED}" "${DISCORD_POST_SHUTDOWN_MESSAGE_URL}"
exit 0

#!/bin/bash
# shellcheck source=scripts/helper_functions.sh
source "/home/steam/server/helper_functions.sh"

# shellcheck source=scripts/negative_delta_recovery.sh
source "/home/steam/server/negative_delta_recovery.sh"

if ! ValidateNegativeDeltaRecoverySetting; then
    LogError "PALWORLD_ALLOW_NEGATIVE_DELTA_TIME must be true or false."
    exit 1
fi

# Remove old FIFO
rm -f "${PalServerLog_fifo}"

if [ "${LOG_FILTER_ENABLED,,}" = true ]; then
    # Recreate FIFO at every boot to avoid stale descriptors and permission drift.
    if ! mkfifo -m 600 "${PalServerLog_fifo}"; then
        echo "ERROR: Failed to create log FIFO: ${PalServerLog_fifo}" >&2
        exit 1
    fi

    # Keep FIFO owned by steam so child processes can always write.
    if [[ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]]; then
        if ! chown steam:steam "${PalServerLog_fifo}"; then
            echo "ERROR: Failed to set log FIFO owner to steam:steam" >&2
            exit 1
        fi
    fi

    exec > >(python3 /home/steam/server/pal_logger.py) 2>&1
fi

mkdir -p /palworld/backups

if [[ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]] && [[ "$(id -g)" -eq 0 ]]; then
    if [[ "${PUID}" -ne 0 ]] && [[ "${PGID}" -ne 0 ]]; then
        LogAction "EXECUTING USERMOD"
        usermod -o -u "${PUID}" steam
        groupmod -o -g "${PGID}" steam
        chown -R steam:steam /palworld /home/steam/
        # NOTE: The recursive chown above covers ${PalServerLog_fifo} under /home/steam,
        # so an explicit second chown/chmod for the FIFO is not required.
    else
        LogError "Running as root is not supported, please fix your PUID and PGID!"
        exit 1
    fi

# Palworld Directory

Everything related to the Palworld data is inside the `/palworld` folder inside the container

## Folder structure

![Folder Structure](../assets/folder_structure.jpg)

| Folder                       | Use                                                               |
|------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|
| palworld                     | Root folder with all the Palworld Server files                    |
| backups                      | Folder where all the backups from the `backup` command are stored |
| Pal/Saved/Config/LinuxServer | Folder with all the .ini configuration files for manual config    |

## Attaching data directory to host filesystem

The simplest way of attaching the palworld folder to your host system is
to use the example given in the compose.yaml file:

```yml
      volumes:
         - ./palworld:/palworld/
```

This creates a `palworld` folder in the current working directory and mounts the `/palworld` folder.

I found comprehensive information on installing BepInEx mods for V Rising dedicated servers. Here's what you need to know:

## Basic Setup Process

V Rising mods use the BepInEx framework. The general installation process involves two main steps:

### 1. Install BepInEx

Download the V Rising BepInExPack from Thunderstore. For Linux servers specifically, grab BepInExPack_V_Rising from Thunderstore (architecture x64), and drop the BepInEx folder plus winhttp.dll and doorstop_config.ini directly in the root, resulting in /home/container/BepInEx/, /home/container/winhttp.dll, and /home/container/doorstop_config.ini. Without winhttp.dll at the root, BepInEx won't inject.

### 2. Install Mods

Place .dll mod files in BepInEx/plugins/. BepInEx loads all .dll files in the Plugins folder automatically on startup.

### 3. Restart Your Server

Restart from Console, and mod configs auto-generate in BepInEx/config/ on first load.

## Finding Mods

Find V Rising mods on Thunderstore or Nexus Mods.

## Important Notes

Bloodstone is the primary server-side modding framework for V Rising. Many server mods depend on it — install Bloodstone first, then mods that require it.

Here are the key steps for installing BepInEx mods on a Sons of the Forest dedicated server:

## Basic Installation Steps

Download BepInEx 5.4.x for your operating system (Windows: BepInEx_win_x64_5.4.x.x.zip or Linux: BepInEx_linux_x64_5.4.x.x.tar.gz), as Sons of the Forest uses a 64-bit Unity build with Mono, not IL2CPP.

Extract the downloaded archive directly into your Sons of the Forest server folder (the same directory containing SonsOfTheForestDS.exe).

## Installing Mods

Upload your mods to the following directory: /BepInEx/plugins. If the "plugins" folder does not exist, you must create it manually. Mods are .dll files that go in BepInEx\plugins.

Individual plugins (DLLs) are dropped into the BepInEx/plugins/ folder and automatically loaded when the server starts.

## Important Considerations

Some mods are server-side only (players don't need them), while others require matching plugin versions on both server and clients. Even with mods installed on the server, the game still requires the client to have manually installed the same mods or have it installed in their Thunderstore mod manager.

Configuration files for mods are found under /BepInEx/config, and you can customize them after the server generates the config files on first startup.

## UE4SS Linux Port Overview

UE4SS now has a Linux-native version that loads straight into your server, enabling you to run UE4SS Lua mods on a Linux Palworld dedicated server without Windows, Proton, or Wine.

Lua mods work out of the box on Linux servers, though mods made for Windows in C++ (.dll files) do not work and need a special Linux build (.so file).

content.content:
# UE4SS Linux — Palworld

A native Linux build of [UE4SS](https://github.com/UE4SS-RE/RE-UE4SS) (Unreal
Engine 4/5 Scripting System) that runs Lua mods on a **Linux dedicated
Palworld server** — no Windows, no Proton, no Wine. Loaded with `LD_PRELOAD`.

> Based on [RE-UE4SS](https://github.com/UE4SS-RE/RE-UE4SS) by UE4SS-RE
> (MIT License), with Palworld fork by
> [Yangff](https://github.com/Yangff) and Linux native port by
> [BlackBookOfficial](https://github.com/BlackBookOfficial/ue4ss-linux-palworld).

## Status

Palworld (UE 5.1) dedicated server: **all major UE4SS hooks verified working
in-game** — BeginPlay, EndPlay, LoadMap, InitGameState, ProcessConsoleExec,
ULocalPlayerExec, EngineTick, ProcessLocalScriptFunction,
CallFunctionByNameWithArguments, UObjectProcessEvent, StaticConstructObject.
`RegisterHook` and Lua mods (e.g. AdminCommands) work as upstream.
Full hook table: [UE4SS-PALWORLD-LINUX-STATUS.md](UE4SS-PALWORLD-LINUX-STATUS.md).

Game updates are handled by three resilience layers — an update either just
works or fails loudly, never silently corrupts the server:

1. **AOB scans** resolve ProcessEvent, FName, GUObjectArray, GMalloc, etc.
   across recompiles.
2. **Self-healing vtable sweep** re-derives AActor BeginPlay/EndPlay slot
   offsets by consensus over all vtables in the binary at boot.
3. **Validation gate** disassembles every vtable hook target before detouring
   and refuses proven-crash signatures with a named log line.

After a server update, boot once and check `UE4SS.log` for `vtable sweep` and
`REFUSED`/`NOTE` lines before anyone joins — details in the status doc.

---

## For Server Owners

### Requirements
- Native Linux Palworld dedicated server (`PalServer-Linux-Shipping`), x86_64
- glibc-based distro (tested on Ubuntu; WSL works)

### Install
Get `libUE4SS.so` — from the [Releases page](../../releases) or a CI artifact
([Actions](../../actions) → latest `Linux & Cross-Compile CI` run), or build
it yourself (below). Then, next to `PalServer.sh`:

```
your-server/
├── PalServer.sh
├── libUE4SS.so              ← the engine hook library
├── UE4SS-settings.ini       ← hook & logging config
├── MemberVariableLayout.ini ← struct offsets (Palworld-specific)
└── Mods/
    ├── mods.txt             ← "ModName : 1" enables a mod
    └── YourMod/
        └── scripts/main.lua
```

Launch with the library preloaded:

```bash
LD_PRELOAD="$PWD/libUE4SS.so" ./PalServer.sh -port=8211 ...your flags...
```

If you use a server manager (AMP, Pterodactyl, a custom script), point its
startup at a wrapper that sets `LD_PRELOAD` and re-creates the symlink after
game updates (managers overwrite the binary).

Verify: `UE4SS.log` appears beside the binary and mods print their load
messages.

### Palworld updates
Just restart. The port re-resolves everything automatically. If a hook ever
fails validation after an update, the server still boots — the hook is
disabled and `UE4SS.log` names it (`Palworld hook validation REFUSED ...`).

---

## For Mod Developers

- **Lua mods**: identical to upstream UE4SS — `Mods/<ModName>/scripts/main.lua`,
  enabled via `Mods/mods.txt`. API docs: upstream
  [UE4SS docs](https://docs.ue4ss.com/). Nothing to port.
- **C++ mods**: must be built as Linux `.so` in `<Mod>/libs/` (not `dlls/`).
  Windows DLLs can never load here.
- Palworld-specifics that differ from upstream:
  - `RegisterKeyBind` needs a real TTY (no stdin console on dedicated servers).
  - GUI runs headless (EGL, hidden window) — no visible window on a server.
  - Console-command mods rely on the `ProcessConsoleExec` hook (works, fires
    on RCON/chat commands).
  - One mod crashing does not kill the server — per-mod crash recovery logs
    and continues.

---

## For Contributors (working on ue4ss-linux)

### How the port works
- **Injection**: `LD_PRELOAD` → `UE4SS/src/main_linux.cpp` bootstraps inside
  the game process (no proxy DLL).
- **Function resolution** (`ScanOverrides`): `dlsym` against the process, then
  port-specific AOB/pattern scans for ProcessEvent, PLSF, CFBNWA, FName,
  StaticConstructObject; heuristics for GUObjectArray/GMalloc — all update-
  robust.
- **JMP thunks**: `RESOLVE_JMP` is thunk-aware (follows mid-function jmp
  stubs) — detouring a stub instead of the real function previously broke
  player joins.
- **Vtable handling** (`deps/first/Unreal/src/UnrealInitializer.cpp`):
  - Palworld's vtables diverge from upstream UE5.1 — per-entry verified
    overrides in the `is_palworld` block (NOT a uniform shift — do not
    blanket-shift, UEngine::Tick proves it).
  - The **vtable sweep** re-derives AActor BeginPlay/EndPlay offsets at boot
    by anchoring on the tick-prerequisite adapter thunk and voting across
    ~500 vtables.
  - The **validation gate** (`validate_hook_target`) prologue-checks every
    vtable hook before install: refuses junk targets and float/int register
    truncation (loud `REFUSED` log), notes shape drift (`NOTE` log) and
    installs anyway — extra pointer args pass through the trampoline safely.
- **Docs to read before changing anything**:
  [UE4SS-PALWORLD-LINUX-STATUS.md](UE4SS-PALWORLD-LINUX-STATUS.md) — hook table,
  verified offsets, crash-signature reading guide, landmines
  (e.g. `VTableLayout.ini` cannot override baked offsets; deploy the `.so`
  atomically). [docs/LINUX_PORT_AUDIT.md](docs/LINUX_PORT_AUDIT.md) —
  classification of all port changes.

### Build
Same recipe CI uses:

```bash
sudo apt-get install -y cmake ninja-build pkg-config gcc g++ \
  libx11-dev libxrandr-dev libxinerama-dev libxcursor-dev libxi-dev \
  libgl-dev libegl-dev libgles-dev
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh

git clone <your-fork-url> && cd ue4ss-linux-palworld
cmake -B build_linux_Dev_gcc -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Game__Dev__Linux64 \
  -DUE4SS_GUI_ENABLED=ON -DUE4SS_INPUT_ENABLED=OFF
cmake --build build_linux_Dev_gcc --target UE4SS
# -> build_linux_Dev_gcc/Game__Dev__Linux64/lib/libUE4SS.so
```

Every push/PR to `linux-native` builds gcc Debug+Dev automatically
([Actions](../../actions)); pushing a `v*` tag publishes a GitHub Release
with the shippable `Dev` build as a ready-to-deploy tarball.

### After a Palworld update
1. Boot once, read `UE4SS.log`: `vtable sweep` lines confirm self-correction,
   `REFUSED` names a disabled hook, `NOTE` flags shape drift.
2. If a slot needs re-derivation, the binary method is in the status doc
   (anchor sweep + caller argument analysis).
3. PRs welcome — keep the per-entry-verification discipline: no blanket
   vtable shifts, verify against the shipping binary.

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE) and [NOTICE](NOTICE). Palworld is a trademark of
Pocketpair, Inc.; this project is not affiliated with or endorsed by them.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about WINEDLLOVERRIDES, winhttp, BepInEx, and Linux Wine configuration:

## Overview

BepInEx works by overriding one of the Windows dll files, in this case the winhttp.dll, allowing BepInEx to run custom code within the game. BepInEx relies on winhttp.dll proxy DLL to inject itself into Unity games.

## WINEDLLOVERRIDES Configuration

If you are using proton with steam, you can specify the DLL override in the launch options: WINEDLLOVERRIDES="winhttp.dll=n,b" %command%. You can skip the winecfg part and put WINEDLLOVERRIDES="winhttp=n,b" %command% in the launch options instead, which does the same thing, just at runtime instead of altering your Proton settings "permanently".

## Alternative Approach with winecfg

If you prefer not to use launch options, in winecfg, select Libraries tab, and under New override for library dropbox, select winhttp and Click add.

## Key Files Required

You will see a few files, a folder named BepInEx, winhttp.dll, etc. that need to be copied to the game's root directory.

content.content:
# ModAPI Mod Installation Method

Based on the documentation, ModAPI uses **IL weaving** to install mods into games. Here's how it works:

## Installation Process

ModAPI patches the game's compiled assemblies through a multi-step process:

1. **Assembly Modification**: The system uses Mono.Cecil to perform IL (Intermediate Language) weaving on the game's managed code. As stated in the architecture section: `"Full Mono.Cecil parse + IL modification + module.Write()"` occurs during the Apply step in Release builds.

2. **Runtime Patching**: Mods are built with .NET 4.8 but get remapped to work with the game's Mono 2.0 runtime. The documentation explains: `"Mod DLL: PE header v4.0.30319, mscorlib 4.0.0.0 → [ModAPI Apply] → modModule.RuntimeVersion = v2.0.50727 → Game Mono 2.0 accepts ✅"`

3. **GUI Requirement**: ModAPI **requires the Windows GUI application** to run the installation. There is no documented command-line or headless mode for applying mods. The process flows through `MainWindow.xaml.cs`'s `ApplyMods()` method, which orchestrates the entire operation including file validation and assembly transformation.

The mod files themselves (`.mod` format) are simply containers; the actual installation is the IL weaving step that modifies the game's assemblies in place.

# ModAchievements Mod Page Overview

**Mod Name & Purpose:**
This page presents ModAchievements, a modification for Green Hell that enables players to "manage game achievements." The mod allows unlocking, resetting, and toggling achievement progress within the game.

**Key Features:**
- Activated via the Alpha9 key (customizable through ModAPI settings)
- Includes multiplayer support with host requirements
- Provides logging capabilities
- Contains a developer debug screen for achievement manipulation

**Download Mechanism:**
The page directs users through a four-step process: download ModAPI, extract files to Program Files, launch ModAPI.exe, enable mods, then start the game. The interface indicates "Your download is ready!" with file extraction instructions.

**Version & Compatibility:**
The latest version is 1.0.0.6 (released September 23, 2024), compatible with Green Hell update U#21.2. The mod file is approximately 30.88 kB.

**Available Resources:**
- Multiple historical versions listed (dating back to November 2020)
- YouTube demo link provided
- FAQ and Discord community links referenced

**No explicit API endpoints** (JSON or direct download URLs) are visible in the provided content; the download appears to be facilitated through the ModAPI Hub interface itself.

RESEARCH COMPLETE. No files edited, no DB writes, no docker pull/run, no VM touched — all read-only WebFetch/WebSearch/curl against public GitHub/Thunderstore/Nexus/CurseForge/Steam sources. One planned live test (querying Nxeon's real MODIO_API_KEY against mod.io's `/games` endpoint) was blocked by this sandbox's own permission layer ("Credential Exploration" denial on reading /opt/nxeon/.env) — flagged at the end, not worked around.

=================================================================
### FAMILY: vrising
=================================================================
**1. Image source**: github.com/TrueOsiris/docker-vrising (`trueosiris/vrising`). Read: `Dockerfile`, `start.sh`, `README.md`. Base `ubuntu:22.04` + wine + steamcmd. No `WORKDIR`/mod `ENV`. Hardcoded in start.sh: `s=/mnt/vrising/server`, `p=/mnt/vrising/persistentdata` — both declared `VOLUME` and both given as `-v` mounts in the prod command (`/opt/vrising/server`, `/opt/vrising/persistentdata`). `VRisingServer.exe` installs into `$s`. **Host path = /opt/vrising/server.**

**2. Image-level mod support**: None. Dockerfile has zero mod ENV. start.sh only handles `GAME_SETTINGS_*`/`HOST_SETTINGS_*` → writes into `ServerGameSettings.json`/`ServerHostSettings.json` via jq. README explicitly has no mod/workshop/BepInEx section.

**3. Game-level mechanism**: V Rising has **no Steam Workshop**. Community mods run on **BepInEx** (Mono doorstop): drop `BepInEx/`, `winhttp.dll`, `doorstop_config.ini` next to `VRisingServer.exe`; plugin `.dll`s go in `BepInEx/plugins/`. (Community-evidence, consistent across Nodecraft/Citadel/G-Portal/AleForge guides.)

**4. Mod source**: Thunderstore community `v-rising`. VERIFIED live: `curl https://thunderstore.io/c/v-rising/api/v1/package/` → **HTTP 200, 301 packages**. Real confirmed packages: `KindredCommands` (odjit) v2.5.8, `BloodyBoss` (Trodi) v2.1.5, `Bloodcraft` (zfolmt) v1.13.22, `Bloodstone` (deca) v0.2.2. Download shape tested: `https://thunderstore.io/package/download/<owner>/<name>/<ver>/` → **HTTP 302** → `https://ccdn.thunderstore.io/live/repository/packages/<owner>-<name>-<ver>.zip`, no auth needed.

**5. steamcmd in container**: YES, `/usr/bin/steamcmd` (symlink to `/usr/games/steamcmd`, VERIFIED in Dockerfile).

**6. Recipe**: extract BepInExPack_V_Rising (Linux/x64) into `/opt/vrising/server/` (BepInEx/, winhttp.dll, doorstop_config.ini next to the exe); plugins into `/opt/vrising/server/BepInEx/plugins/`. **Open risk**: start.sh never sets `WINEDLLOVERRIDES`, and Wine's default DLL search order does not reliably let an app-local `winhttp.dll` win over Wine's builtin one — TrueOsiris/docker-vrising issue #45 ("How to get BepInEx to work") exists precisely because of this. Likely needs a container recreate adding `-e WINEDLLOVERRIDES=winhttp=n,b`. Confirm via `BepInEx/LogOutput.log` under `/opt/vrising/server/BepInEx/` showing the injection banner + "Loading [<Plugin>]" lines.

**7. Example mods**: Bloodstone (deca) v0.2.2 — the base modding framework, smallest/simplest load-only test. BloodyBoss (Trodi) v2.1.5. KindredCommands (odjit) v2.5.8.

**8. Verdict**: REAL-MECHANISM (download-and-place). Confidence: **MEDIUM** — mechanism/source solid; the WINEDLLOVERRIDES interaction for this specific image is unverified (no live test performed, per the "don't touch any VM" constraint).

=================================================================
### FAMILY: sonsoftheforest
=================================================================
**1. Image source**: github.com/jammsen/docker-sons-of-the-forest-dedicated-server. Read: `Dockerfile`, `entrypoint.sh`, `scripts/servermanager.sh`, `configs/dedicatedserver.cfg.example`. Base `cm2network/steamcmd:root@sha256:e6b6...` (pinned) + WineHQ stable on Debian trixie. `GAME_PATH="/sonsoftheforest"` (single `VOLUME`, matches prod `-v /opt/sonsoftheforest:/sonsoftheforest`). `SonsOfTheForestDS.exe` installed via `+force_install_dir "$GAME_PATH" ... +app_update 2465200`. **Host path = /opt/sonsoftheforest.**

**2. Image-level mod support**: None. Full ENV block quoted from Dockerfile: `GAME_PATH, GAME_USERDATA_PATH, GAME_CONFIGFILE_PATH, STEAMCMD_PATH, WINEDATA_PATH, WINEARCH, WINEPREFIX, DISPLAY, TIMEZONE, PUID, PGID, FILTER_SHADER_AND_MESH_AND_WINE_DEBUG, ALWAYS_UPDATE_ON_START, SKIP_NETWORK_ACCESSIBILITY_TEST` — no mod var anywhere. `servermanager.sh` only does install/update/start/stop, no mod logic.

**3. Game-level mechanism**: BepInEx, **IL2CPP** variant (SOTF is IL2CPP Unity) — Thunderstore's `BepInExPack_IL2CPP` has 563 dependents in this community. Same drop-beside-exe mechanism.

**4. Mod source**: Thunderstore community `sons-of-the-forest`. VERIFIED live: **HTTP 200, 81 packages**, community metadata shows `total_download_count: 2,269,058`. Confirmed real packages: `BepInExPack_IL2CPP` (BepInEx) v6.0.755, `BepInExConfigurationManagerIL2CPP` (crossi) v18.3.0, `BepInEx_ConfigurationManager` (faulty) v1.3.1, `AdminMenu` (pineapple54). Download tested for `BepInExPack_IL2CPP` 6.0.755: 302 → ccdn CDN zip, no auth. This reconfirms Nxeon's existing 73-row `source=thunderstore` catalogue is pointed at a real, live source.

**5. steamcmd**: YES, `$STEAMCMD_PATH="/home/steam/steamcmd"` (VERIFIED, Dockerfile ENV + used in servermanager.sh).

**6. Recipe**: extract `BepInExPack_IL2CPP` contents directly into `/opt/sonsoftheforest/` (next to the exe); plugins into `/opt/sonsoftheforest/BepInEx/plugins/`. `ALWAYS_UPDATE_ON_START=true` means steamcmd `app_update ... validate` runs every boot — `validate` only checks depot-manifest files, so extra BepInEx files should survive (consistent with this already working in prod). Same WINEDLLOVERRIDES caveat as vrising exists in principle in this image's own scripts too (not set anywhere I could find) — but since Nxeon already runs 73 live Thunderstore mods for this family, their actual worker must already handle it one way or another; I flag this as **verify-against-the-real-worker-code**, not a new gap I'm asserting exists. Confirm via `BepInEx/LogOutput.log`.

**7. Example mods**: `BepInExConfigurationManagerIL2CPP` (crossi) and `BepInEx_ConfigurationManager` (faulty) — pure config-UI utilities, zero gameplay effect, ideal load-only smoke tests. `AdminMenu` (pineapple54) — real gameplay-utility mod.

**8. Verdict**: REAL-MECHANISM (download-and-place), already live in prod. Confidence: **HIGH**.

=================================================================
### FAMILY: sunkenland
=================================================================
**1. Image source**: github.com/melle2/sunkenland-ds (`melle2/sunkenland-ds`). Read: `Dockerfile`, `startSunkenland.sh`. Base `melle2/wine-steamcmd-ubuntu:24.04-3`. `USER_NAME=sunkenland`, `APP_ID=2667530`. Game installs to `/${USER_NAME}/game` = `/sunkenland/game` (Dockerfile `mkdir ${USER_NAME}/game`; startSunkenland.sh `steamcmd +force_install_dir /${USER_NAME}/game ... +app_update "${APP_ID}"`) — matches prod `-v /opt/sunkenland/game:/sunkenland/game`. **Host path = /opt/sunkenland/game.**

**2. Image-level mod support**: None. Dockerfile ENV: `USER_NAME, APP_ID, WORLD_FOLDER, WINEDEBUG, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` only. startSunkenland.sh reads only `GAME_WORLD_GUID, GAME_REGION, GAME_MAX_PLAYER, GAME_SESSION_INVISIBLE, GAME_UPDATE, GAME_BETA_VERSION, GAME_PASSWORD` — no mod var.

**3. Game-level mechanism**: BepInEx (Mono, non-IL2CPP — package is named `BepInExPack_Sunkenland` not `_IL2CPP`). Same drop-beside-exe mechanism, target = `Sunkenland-DedicatedServer.exe`.

**4. Mod source**: Thunderstore community `sunkenland`. VERIFIED live: **HTTP 200, 45 packages**. Confirmed real: `BepInExPack_Sunkenland` (SunkenlandModding) v5.4.22, `SunkenCompass` (Azumatt) v1.0.2, `BepInEx_ConfigurationManager` (Azumatt) v18.0.1, plus `FullRecycle`/`BaseRaidTimer`/`ModSettingsMenu` published by `Ice_Box_Studio_Sunkenland` (appears to be the actual dev studio account). Download tested for both `BepInExPack_Sunkenland` 5.4.22 and `SunkenCompass` 1.0.2: both 302 → ccdn CDN zip, no auth. Reconfirms Nxeon's existing 22-row `source=thunderstore` catalogue.

**5. steamcmd**: Present (base image `melle2/wine-steamcmd-ubuntu:24.04-3` ships it, invoked as bare `steamcmd` on PATH in startSunkenland.sh) — exact absolute path not visible in this repo's own files (baked into the upstream base image), so reported as **VERIFIED-present / exact path UNKNOWN**.

**6. Recipe**: extract `BepInExPack_Sunkenland` into `/opt/sunkenland/game/`; plugins into `/opt/sunkenland/game/BepInEx/plugins/`. Notably **safer than the other three Wine-based families**: the update guard is `if [ "$GAME_UPDATE" = true ] || [ -z "$(ls -A /sunkenland/game)" ]` — once the folder is non-empty and `GAME_UPDATE` isn't explicitly `true`, steamcmd does **not** re-run on every boot, so mod files are not at risk from any update pass at all. A plain restart (no recreate) is enough, unless WINEDLLOVERRIDES also needs adding here (untested, same caveat as vrising). Confirm via `BepInEx/LogOutput.log` under `/opt/sunkenland/game/BepInEx/`.

**7. Example mods**: `SunkenCompass` (Azumatt) — tiny QoL. `BepInEx_ConfigurationManager` (Azumatt) — utility only. `ModSettingsMenu` (Ice_Box_Studio_Sunkenland) — from the apparent official dev account.

**8. Verdict**: REAL-MECHANISM (download-and-place), already live in prod. Confidence: **HIGH**.

=================================================================
### FAMILY: theforest
=================================================================
**1. Image source**: github.com/jammsen/docker-the-forest-dedicated-server. Read: `Dockerfile`, `entrypoint.sh`, `scripts/servermanager.sh`, `configs/server.cfg.example`. Same base pattern as sonsoftheforest (`cm2network/steamcmd:root` + WineHQ). `GAME_PATH="/theforest"` (matches prod `-v /opt/theforest:/theforest`). `TheForestDedicatedServer.exe` via `+force_install_dir "$GAME_PATH" ... +app_update 556450`. **Host path = /opt/theforest** (saves at `/opt/theforest/saves`, config at `/opt/theforest/config`, same mount).

**2. Image-level mod support**: None. Full ENV block: `GAME_PATH, GAME_SAVEGAME_PATH, GAME_CONFIG_PATH, GAME_CONFIGFILE_PATH, STEAMCMD_PATH, THEFOREST_TEMPLATE_FILE, WINEDATA_PATH, WINEARCH, WINEPREFIX, DISPLAY, PUID, PGID, TIMEZONE, SERVER_SETTINGS_MODE, FILTER_SHADER_AND_MESH_AND_WINE_DEBUG, ALWAYS_UPDATE_ON_START, SERVER_STEAM_ACCOUNT_TOKEN, SERVER_NAME, ADMIN_PASSWORD, SERVER_PASSWORD` — zero mod vars. `servermanager.sh` has no mod logic.

**3. Game-level mechanism — the key negative finding**: The Forest does **not** use BepInEx (confirmed: no `thunderstore.io/c/the-forest` community exists — `curl https://thunderstore.io/api/cyberstorm/community/?page_size=200` lists `sons-of-the-forest` but nothing for `the-forest`, and a direct `curl https://thunderstore.io/c/the-forest/api/v1/package/` returned `{"error": "No cache available"}`, i.e. no such community). Its actual community tool is **ModAPI** (fluffyfishgames/ModAPI, hub at modapi.survivetheforest.net), and ModAPI works fundamentally differently from BepInEx: it performs **IL weaving** — reading GitHub's own repo docs (fetched in full): *"Full Mono.Cecil parse + IL modification + module.Write()"* rewrites the game's compiled `Assembly-CSharp.dll` directly, and this step is driven exclusively by ModAPI's **Windows WPF GUI app** (`MainWindow.xaml.cs`'s `ApplyMods()`); **no command-line/headless install path is documented anywhere in the repo.**

**4. Mod source**: modapi.survivetheforest.net is the only dedicated-server-relevant mod source. It DOES list `[DS]`-tagged mods specifically for "The Forest Dedicated Server" — confirmed present on the live page `modapi.survivetheforest.net/game/TheForestDedicatedServer/`: **"[DS] Command Console"**, **"[DS] Players List"**, **"[DS] Ban List"**. But per (3), applying any of these to a running server means producing a patched `Assembly-CSharp.dll` via that GUI tool — not moving a file into a folder.

**5. steamcmd**: YES, `$STEAMCMD_PATH="/home/steam/steamcmd"` (VERIFIED, same as sonsoftheforest).

**6. Recipe**: **None fits Nxeon's model.** SSH+curl+docker-exec+env-recreate can move files and flip env vars; it cannot drive a Windows WPF GUI app through an IL-weaving workflow. This is a structural gap, not a "didn't look hard enough" gap — it's sourced directly from ModAPI's own architecture documentation.

**7. Example mods that exist for the DS target (not deployable today)**: "[DS] Command Console", "[DS] Players List", "[DS] Ban List" (all confirmed present on the live ModAPI Hub game page).

**8. Verdict**: **NONE**, for Nxeon's current automation model — this is a genuinely "no viable one-click mechanism" finding, distinct from "the game has zero mods." If Nxeon wants this later, the real ask is either replicating ModAPI's Mono.Cecil weaving headlessly (high effort, unsupported by upstream) or running the actual ModAPI.exe unattended under Wine+Xvfb (untested, WPF apps are fragile under Wine headless). Confidence: **HIGH** that no simple mechanism exists.

### FAMILY: palworld
=================================================================
**1. Image source**: github.com/thijsvanloef/palworld-server-docker.
